report.incident_title: Checkout failures ~20% since shortly after 14:00 UTC
report.summary: Since the checkout-svc v2.14.0 deploy at 14:01Z (rolled to 100% by 14:04), checkout 5xx rate rose from about 0.3% to about 21-22% (E1, E20), and the CheckoutErrorRateHigh alert fired at 14:08Z (E7). Confirmed by tool data: the failing requests carry a TypeError at formatPrice (src/pricing/format.ts:41) reading 'code' of undefined, on carts with cart_schema=v1 (E3, E25); the successful trace for a v2 cart passes through the same function (E5, E26); and the v2.14.0 change reads cart.currency.code instead of a global default (E12, E36). No infra events, payments-svc 5xx (flat at 0.1%), or orders-db latency change coincide with the onset (E8, E16, E22, E24). Assumptions, not observed: that every v1 cart fails and that the failure share equals the v1 cart share of 22.4% (E6). Only four formatPrice errors appear in logs for 11:00-14:30, which is far fewer than a 21% failure rate would produce, and no currency or locale breakdown was obtainable (E9), so the currency-clustering test is incomplete. The catalog-svc deploy at 11:20 is not linked to checkout (E28), but its effect was not measured because metrics start at 13:30 (E29).
report.root_cause: The checkout-svc v2.14.0 change to formatPrice (multi-currency price formatting, deployed 14:01Z) reads cart.currency.code with no guard. Carts on schema v1 do not have a currency object, so the read of 'code' on undefined throws a TypeError inside pricing.formatPrice (E3, E12, E25). The exception is not handled, so checkout returns a 5xx and the customer sees 'Something went wrong'. Successful v2 carts do not hit this error (E5, E26). The share of failing requests matching the v1 cart share (~22%, E6) is a correlation that has not been confirmed per request, and the log count is much lower than the error rate, so the exact failing population is not fully established.

hypotheses.statement: The v2.14.0 multi-currency price formatting change introduced an unguarded read of cart.currency.code, causing a TypeError on carts using schema v1 (those without currency.code), affecting ~22% of checkouts with v1 carts and resulting in 5xx errors.

corrective_actions.action: Roll checkout-svc back from v2.14.0 to v2.13.2 using deployctl rollback checkout-svc --to v2.13.2 (runbook rb-rollback), then confirm the 5xx rate returns to baseline within 5 minutes. Confirm first that checkout-svc is stateless, as the runbook assumes, since this is not verified in the data.
corrective_actions.rationale: The regression is tied to the 14:01 deploy and nothing else changed in the window (E13, E14). Rollback is the fastest way to stop the errors. The runbook says rollback is safe for stateless services (E19).

corrective_actions.action: Add a guard in formatPrice so a missing cart.currency falls back to the previous default currency, and add unit and integration tests for schema v1 carts. Re-deploy only after those tests pass.
corrective_actions.rationale: The stack trace shows the failure is an unguarded property access on a missing field (E3, E25). The same class of bug caused PIR-2026-031 (E17), so a guard plus tests addresses the defect itself.

corrective_actions.action: Require a canary or staged rollout for checkout-svc with error-rate gating on v1 and v2 cart traffic, and add contract or schema-compatibility tests against cart schema v1 before release. Accelerate the v1 to v2 cart migration tracked in CART-212 so that the legacy path is smaller.
corrective_actions.rationale: The deploy went to 100% in about three minutes (14:01 to 14:04, E12), so no gate caught the regression. The v1 carts that remain are the trigger (E6).

corrective_actions.action: Alert on the formatPrice TypeError signature and on checkout 5xx split by cart_schema and currency. Add the currency and locale labels that the metrics and logs currently lack, so failure clustering can be tested directly.
corrective_actions.rationale: The currency and label breakdown returned no series (E9), and the error logs carry no currency or locale attributes. The current signal only showed the aggregate rate, so the cause was found late.
